title: Here’s Why Fifth Harmony Fans Think the Girl Group Is Making a Comeback Ahead of Anniversary
summary: The girl group formed almost exactly 14 years ago.
contentText:
It looks like Fifth Harmony is planning to make its upcoming anniversary worth it for fans, with the girl group teasing a surprise on Instagram that some Harmonizers think might be a full-fledged comeback.

Related

Zara Larsson Addresses Rumor She Was Asked to Replace Camila Cabello in Fifth Harmony

Fifth Harmony Surprises Fans With Reunion Performance at Jonas Brothers Show in Dallas

Here’s Camila Cabello’s Reaction to Fifth Harmony’s Reunion After Seven Years

In a joint post on social media by Fifth Harmony Shop and former members Ally Brooke, Dinah Jane and Lauren Jauregui, the ladies shared a simple black poster reading, simply, “Fifth Harmony.”

“happy birthday to us,” the caption read. “next week.”

The open-ended post leaves room for a lot of speculation as to what the band is teasing, and a lot of fans are wondering whether it’s a reunion in the works. “a rumored fifth harmony comeback im not just sat baby im the whole chair,” one person wrote on X .

Journalist Tomas Mier, however, wrote on X that the teaser is simply for “a merch drop celebrating the anniversary,” but added that Fifth Harmony did recently sign with UTA talent agent Mike G, possibly indicating that something more is in the works.

Billboard has reached out to reps for the girl group members and UTA for comment.

Fifth Harmony first formed in July 2012, making it almost exactly 14 years since the former quintet was assembled on X Factor . The original lineup consisted of Brooke, Jane, Jauregui, Normani and Camila Cabello, becoming a foursome after Cabello left the group in December 2016 to pursue a solo career. By the time the quartet disbanded in 2018, the members had notched eight hits on the Billboard Hot 100 — including No. 4 smash “Work From Home” — and five entries on the Billboard 200 .

In August last year, Brooke, Jane, Jauregui and Normani reunited on stage for the first time in seven years at a Jonas Brothers concert in Dallas.
